chunks: What Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿid, from Yunus ibn Yaʿqub, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him):

He said: I heard him say: "I shrouded my father in two shatawi garments in which he used to enter the state of ihram, and in a shirt from his shirts, and in a turban that had belonged to ʿAli ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and in a burd which I had purchased for forty dinars — had it been valued today, it would be worth four hundred dinars."

Because the [correct] interpretation of this report is [that it pertains to] a circumstance in which cotton cannot be obtained; moreover, it is a narration of an action, and it is possible that this was specific to them (peace be upon them). He did not say therein 'you ought to do the same.' And when this is not [stated] in it, following it is not obligatory.

key_terms.الْقُطْنِ: cotton — the prescribed standard material for the burial kafan in Shia fiqh
key_terms.حِكَايَةُ: narration of an action — a uṣūl al-fiqh category: a reported act that does not carry the binding force of an explicit verbal ruling
key_terms.شَطَوِيَّيْنِ: two shatawi garments — linen cloth woven in Shata (Egypt), traditionally used as ihram garments
key_terms.كَفَّنْتُ: I shrouded — the act of wrapping the deceased in a burial kafan (shroud)

ai.seo_question: What materials did Imam al-Kazim (AS) use to shroud Imam al-Sadiq (AS), and how does Shaykh al-Tusi reconcile this with the ruling that the kafan must be made of cotton?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) reports that he personally shrouded his father, Imam al-Sadiq (AS), using non-cotton materials: two shatawi garments used for ihram, a shirt, a turban inherited from Imam al-Sajjad (AS), and a costly burd. Shaykh al-Tusi then interprets this as an exception confined to circumstances where cotton is unobtainable, further noting that since it is merely a narrated action possibly specific to the Imams (AS), it carries no binding legal obligation for others.
